html:
Kali is the name the map gives, in its 1715 snapshot, to a small territory in what is now western Mali, between the upper Senegal River and the Niger. No state of that name is well known; the label may be a slip for one of the Malinke or Bambara chiefdoms of the area.

Around 1715 this land lay between the shrunken Mali Empire to the south, the rising Bambara kingdom of Segou on the Niger, and the lands where the Kaarta kingdom would soon take shape. Its people were mostly farmers growing millet and sorghum, and the region sent captives west to the European posts on the Senegal River.
